decisions.diagnosis: The South channel also registered northbound riders for two weeks, so South read roughly South plus North while North stayed normal.
decisions.evidence: South/North daily ratio 1.7-1.95 against a rolling median of 0.79; South minus North = 150-285/day, matching normal South levels (180-230); South's hourly profile gains North's PM peak (48/h vs 17/h in March); ends abruptly by 2013-03-02 (S 41 < N 59).

decisions.diagnosis: The failing counter undercounted heavily (North worst) between intermittent outages, while the neighbouring counter 0.3 km away (site 176) was steady.
decisions.evidence: Daily 107/176 total ratio 0.26-0.58 (normal 0.8-0.9); complete weeks 2016-02-29 and 03-07 total 1717 and 1380 vs ~3500 in 2015 while site 176 held ~4000/week; North/South split flipped (S/N 1.4-1.6 vs 0.86).

decisions.diagnosis: Final days before the counter died: undercounting, then a corrupt burst of hundreds per slot on 2017-01-23 ahead of the impossible counts on 2017-01-27.
decisions.evidence: 107/176 ratio 0.27-0.52 on 2017-01-14..20; 2017-01-23 11:30-13:00 slots of 109-618 (North 2769, South 1532 in 1.5 h on a Monday with no event at site 176); 2017-01-27 already flagged impossible_count (6385/9221).

decisions.diagnosis: The counter ran intermittently in this period (recurring Friday gaps, mostly partial days), and some complete days read low against the neighbour, so the remaining complete days may undercount.
After the counter was reinstated in May 2018 the North and South labels are swapped relative to 2011-2016 and 2021-2026; the total is unaffected.
decisions.evidence: In 2011-15 and 2021-26 South carries the AM peak (24-25/h at 06-07h) and North the PM peak (21-26/h at 16-17h); in 2018-19 it is the reverse (North AM 24-26/h, South PM 23/h). North>South in all other years but South>North by ~1.2x throughout 2018-19. The October ride spike that matches site 176 direction 112 lands on 107 North in 2016 but on 107 South in 2018 and 2019.

summary: Single piezo counter on the John Whitton Bridge path, 2011-2026, with long gaps in 2015-2018 and 2020-2021; the automatic fixes (zero outages, the 2022-02-19 halving) check out against the neighbouring site 176. The main problems are a two-week 2013 fault where South also counted northbound riders, a failing counter in 2015-12 to 2017-01 that undercounted and then produced corrupt bursts, and swapped direction labels for 2018-05 to 2019-12. October spikes are real organised rides.
